They are used to slow the heart rate in supraventricular arrhythmias, especially atrial fibrillation, and are also given in chronic heart failure. Described in this chapter are Acetyldigoxin, p.1201 Digoxin, p.1259 Deslanoside, p.1257 Lanatoside C, p.1322 Digitalis Lanata Leaf, Metildigoxin, p.1336 p.1258 Ouabain, p.1364 Digitalis Leaf, p.1258 Proscillaridin, p.1382 Digitoxin, p.1259 Strophanthin-K, p.1406 ◊ Phosphodiesterase inhibitors are potent inotropes; they also have vasodilator effects. They are used in the short- term treatment of severe heart failure; long-term oral ther- apy with some phosphodiesterase inhibitors has been asso- ciated with increased mortality. Described in this chapter are Amrinone, p.1215 Olprinone, p.1361 Enoximone, p.1278 Pimobendan, p.1371 Milrinone, p.1341 Vesnarinone, p.1425 Centrally acting antihypertensives Centrally acting antihypertensives include alpha2-adreno- ceptor agonists such as clonidine and methyldopa. Stimu- lation of alpha2 adrenoceptors in the CNS results in a re- duction in sympathetic tone and a fall in blood pressure. Heart rate is also reduced. They are used in the manage- ment of hypertension, although other drugs with fewer Cardiovascular Drugs 1155 The symbol † denotes a preparation no longer actively marketed The symbol  denotes a substance whose use may be restricted in certain sports (see p.vii) adverse effects are generally preferred. Apraclonidine (p.1877) and brimonidine (p.1878) are alpha2-adrenocep- tor agonists that are used in the management of glaucoma. Described in this chapter are Clonidine, p.1247 Methyldopa, p.1334 Guanabenz, p.1299 Moxonidine, p.1345 Guanfacine, p.1301 Rilmenidine, p.1388 Diuretics Diuretics promote the excretion of water and electrolytes by the kidneys. They are used in the treatment of heart fail- ure or in hepatic, renal, or pulmonary disease when salt and water retention has resulted in oedema or ascites. Diu- retics are also used, either alone, or in association with oth- er drugs, in the treatment of hypertension, although the mechanism for their antihypertensive effect is poorly un- derstood.
